route: route 1/8 hybrid: intercorrelation-signature replication across the CPC-12's two development samples + external-criterion ordering
evidence: Route: cross-sample replication of the CPC-12 hope items' asymmetric intercorrelation signature, plus an independent external-criterion ordering. (A) In the instrument's own two development samples the three pairwise correlations are all distinct and ordered r(1,2) < r(1,3) < r(2,3): Lorenz 2016 S1 Dataset (n=321, SHS columns hope1/hope4/hope5) = 0.313 / 0.474 / 0.584, and S2 Dataset (n=202, cpc1/cpc2/cpc3) = 0.342 / 0.499 / 0.545. The live table (n=1,010 complete triples) gives r(Hope_1,Hope_2)=0.456, r(Hope_1,Hope_3)=0.581, r(Hope_2,Hope_3)=0.639 - the same strict ordering. Because S3 acts faithfully on the three pairs, exactly 1 of the 6 possible assignments reproduces it, so every item is separated from every other, not just grouped (p=0.167 by chance). (B) An independent statistic selects the same permutation: in Lorenz S2 the 'pretty successful' item correlates 0.368 with the life-satisfaction mean vs 0.211 (item 3) and 0.162 (item 1), predicting H2 > H3 > H1 against well-being; in the Pellerin data that ordering holds in 7 of 8 wave x criterion comparisons (wave 0: EWB .257/.529/.368, PWB .356/.490/.449, SWB .202/.408/.317, IWB .283/.533/.375; wave 5: EWB .442/.610/.548, SWB .267/.450/.396, IWB .271/.553/.394), the single exception being wave-5 PWB where H3=.583 edges H2=.570. Two independent 1-in-6 tests agree on the same unique assignment. What this does NOT establish: it is a structural match, not a source-level label tie - the OSF deposit is a bare CSV with no variable labels, so no file anywhere states the Hope_k <-> item-k correspondence, and the route assumes the German development samples' item structure carries to this French administration.
